problem: Image-goal navigation SOTA relies on odometry (GPS+compass), RL trained for 10-100M steps in simulators, or topological graphs and metric maps. These become unusable or costly when odometry is unavailable.
motivation: Humans navigate unseen places without detailed metric maps, so a lightweight memory that only records what has been seen might suffice. The paper asks whether a learned latent 'memory proxy' plus imitation of human waypoint choices can replace odometry, graphs and RL, while training on far less data.
key_idea: A three-tier feudal agent (memory proxy map manager, human-imitating waypoint network, classifier worker) uses a self-supervised 2D latent density map of visited views as memory, with no RL, graph, odometry or metric map.
insight: The Gaussian-weighted MPM is the key component: adding any MPM gives about +25% and the Gaussian density version beats binary versions by about 28% (Table 2 ablation). The feature space must preserve relative distances: SMoG features resemble the ground-truth distance matrix more than MoCo, ResNet or SwAV. Using Superglue keypoint clusters as positive pairs gives this odometry-free distance preservation. The learned classifier worker adds a further ~10% over the deterministic one.
method: High-level manager (MPM): a SMoG contrastive encoder (128-d) trained with positive pairs sampled from Superglue keypoint-match clusters of images along human trajectories, so feature distance approximates spatial distance without odometry.

Isomap imitator: a 2-layer MLP regresses isomap 2D embeddings from SMoG features. At test time each observation is placed on a 2D map and a Gaussian window (sigma=1) is added, giving a density map of exploration. The map is local, fixed-size and cropped around the latest position.
Mid-level manager (WayNet): a ResNet-18 modified to take 7-channel input (RGBD + MPM crop). It is trained on LAVN human point-click trajectories to predict a pixel waypoint.
Goal-directed switching: Superglue keypoint matches between the current view and the goal image replace the waypoint with the mean matched keypoint when confidence is high (alpha_k=0.7).

Low-level worker: a 4-layer PReLU MLP with separate projection heads for the depth map and the waypoint. It classifies among turn left 15°, turn right 15° and forward 0.25 m, trained on human actions from LAVN.
Stop rule: stop when goal-match confidence is high (0.7) and depth is ≤1 m, or the matched-keypoint area ratio exceeds 0.85.

setting.backbone: SMoG encoder + MLP isomap imitator + ResNet-18 (7-channel) WayNet + MLP action classifier, all trained; Superglue used for keypoint matching
setting.training_data: Subset of the LAVN human point-click navigation dataset: 117 trajectories, 36,834 frames (~37K images); no RL and no simulator training; total ~3M iterations
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (480x640, 120° FOV) + goal image; no GPS/compass
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: turn left 15°, turn right 15°, move forward 0.25 m
setting.simulator: Habitat with Gibson (evaluation only; training uses recorded human data)

numbers.eval_set_note: NRNS protocol, ~6K start-goal pairs from 14 unseen Gibson environments; straight trajectories, average over easy/medium/hard
numbers.extra: trained on 117 LAVN human trajectories (~37K frames); no odometry, no RL; 500 step limit, 1 m success radius
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (straight, FeudalNav Ours): Average Succ 67.5, SPL 55.5; ablation table shows 67.54 / 55.52

numbers.eval_set_note: NRNS protocol; curved trajectories, average over easy/medium/hard
numbers.extra: trained on 117 LAVN human trajectories (~37K frames); no odometry, no RL; 500 step limit, 1 m success radius
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (curved, FeudalNav Ours): Average Succ 60.2, SPL 39.1

numbers_note: Ablation variants (Table 2) exist, e.g. without MPM and with deterministic worker, but only the main method is listed. Gibson test environments are the NRNS unseen split.
results: FeudalNav reaches 67.5 SR / 55.5 SPL on straight and 60.2 SR / 39.1 SPL on curved Gibson image-goal episodes. This beats NRNS+SLING (64.4/50.8 straight; 43.7/14.3 curved) and OVRL+SLING (58.2/42.5; 55.4/37.4). It does so without odometry, RL or graphs, using ~37K training images versus 3.5M for NRNS and 14.5M for OVRL.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation on Gibson image-goal; no real-robot tests and no other benchmarks.
Depends on Superglue keypoint matching and hand-chosen confidence thresholds for goal detection and stopping.
Depends on the LAVN human-teleoperation dataset, and the MPM is a coarse 2D isomap approximation that does not give real localization.
